chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Ṭālib ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Qāsim ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, a man prostrates on his sleeve because of the harm of heat and cold. He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the authority giving the ruling
key_terms.كُمِّهِ: his sleeve, the cloth on which sajdah is being performed
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it, indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَسْجُدُ: performs sajdah, meaning prostrates in prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sajdah on one's sleeve because of severe heat or cold?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام concerning sajdah in conditions of hardship. He permits a person to prostrate on his sleeve when harmed by intense heat or cold, indicating allowance in such circumstances.
